accuracy.evidence: Checked 616 against CCSS 1.NBT.3 (compare two two-digit numbers based on tens and ones digits, record with >, =, <) and NC Y2 NPV (compare and order numbers from 0 to 100; use <, > and =). Worked by hand: 34 < 43 (3 tens vs 4); 58 > 52 (same tens, ones 8 > 2); 47 < 74; 70 > 69; 55 = 55; order 29, 58, 71.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented slips: digit-sum equality (3+4 = 4+3 so 34 and 43 'match'), reading a number backwards (34 as 43), choosing by glyph height, opening > toward the smaller number, and treating 40 as equal to 4. Lab myth step and challenge feedback name each slip.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcmp2d teaches tens-first then ones comparison with > = < slots and a three-number order drag; flagcmpnum only covers numerals 1–10, flag2digit builds tens/ones without comparison symbols, flagmore is concrete more/less without two-digit place value. Lab gate shingle overlap under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees tens rods vs ones cubes for 34 and 43, picks why more tens wins, chooses < for 47 ? 74, drags 29/58/71 into order, and rejects the digit-sum myth — discovering the rule before the text restates it.

predictions.evidence: Six predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: '34 greater because ones look bigger', digit-sum equality, wrong symbol for 47 ? 74, reverse order 71/58/29, and '40 = 4'.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Challenge asks which symbol fits a ? b. Wrong tags get distinct messages: flip (digit reversal), sum (digit-sum myth), opp (symbol facing the wrong way), eq (equal used when tens differ).

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and Y2 terms: tens, ones, greater, less, equal, > = <. Adult names the standards and four mistakes. Family audience targets keep FK within lesson limits.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate found no filler phrases. Each kid paragraph states one rule (places, tens first, ones next, symbols); adult gives standard, rule, mistakes and lab actions.

mobile.evidence: Young layout with big number cards, three symbol pads, and three order slots sized for 390 px; every drag has a Pick/Put button twin; nothing relies on hover.

accessibility.evidence: Button twins for every compare, symbol and order action; canvas aria-label updated with each speak(); walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA expected clean in both themes.

sources: CCSS Math 1.NBT.3: compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, and <
